subject: Hyperscale dedicated sizing: commitment / burst matrix and sharding inventory
messages:
From: Daniel Wang <daniel@hyperscale.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ops Eng Team <ops@hyperscale.ai>
Date: Sun, 13 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Hyperscale dedicated sizing — request for commitment/burst matrix and sharding inventory

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team is excited about Redwood's routing and fallback story. We're moving toward an internal decision on reserved capacity and need a concrete pre-sales intake so we can align procurement + infra. Two asks to start:

1) Can you send your pre-sales questionnaire focused on commitment vs burst allowance, session lifecycle (session pins, idle timeouts), and GPU sharding/tiling guidance? We want to map our 90-day traffic plan to your capacity models.

2) We'll attach a small sample of our production traffic (anonymized) — mostly short chat completions and few long generation jobs. Would appreciate guidance on GPU mix and suggested oversubscription.

Procurement will want clear SLAs for latency p95/p99 and any overage billing semantics. Copying procurement and ops.

Best,
Daniel
Director of Platform Engineering
Hyperscale.ai

Attachment: none (will reply with sample CSV)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Wang <daniel@hyperscale.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Hyperscale dedicated sizing — request for commitment/burst matrix and sharding inventory

Hi Daniel — great to hear and glad the demo landed. Attaching a concise pre-sales questionnaire that focuses precisely on the items you called out: commitment vs burst, session lifecycle, prompt/response length distributions, and recommended GPU tiling/sharding for mixed workloads.

High level next steps:
- You fill the attached "pre-sales-questionnaire.pdf" and include the sample CSV with token-level histograms if possible.
- Karthik and I will convert that into a proposed GPU mix and a commitment/burst matrix that shows expected sustained commit, burst headroom, and suggested autoscaling policy.
- We'll include explicit p95/p99 latency projections for the proposed mix plus fallback options (quantized variants, region fallbacks).

A few clarifying questions to help us size conservatively:
1) Of your calls, what percent are streaming (partial response streaming) vs full-response generation?
2) Do you have any strict KV-cache affinity needs (session pinning) or can we treat sessions as ephemeral and rely on prefix caching?
3) Are embeddings used as a background job (batch) or inline with user requests?

I'll call out where we need sample fields in the questionnaire. Ben, can you grab the latest shard-efficiency matrix for 80B/33B mixes and add to the drive link?

Thanks — attaching questionnaire now.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachment: pre-sales-questionnaire.pdf (pdf)
Link: https://drive.redwood/reports/hs_preflight

From: Daniel Wang <daniel@hyperscale.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ops Eng Team <ops@hyperscale.ai>, procurement@hyperscale.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 08:37:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Hyperscale dedicated sizing — request for commitment/burst matrix and sharding inventory

Hi Marissa — attached is our anonymized sample (hyperscale_workload_sample.csv) and a quick pass at the questionnaire. Quick answers inline below and in the attached doc:

- Streaming vs full-response: ~75% short streaming completions (assistant-style, mean response length ~45 tokens), ~20% standard full-response completions (mean ~220 tokens), ~5% long-form generation jobs (mean ~1,400 tokens) usually run as scheduled batch jobs.
- Session affinity: low. We prefer ephemeral sessions with prefix caching — only a small subset (~8%) of requests rely on strict per-session KV.
- Embeddings: mostly batch (nightly vectorization for 2M-doc corpus) but a small fraction (~3%) are inline for similarity search.
- Peak pattern: we have a primary US peak 11:00-14:00 PST with a smaller evening peak 18:00-20:00 PST. Dayparting ratio peak:sustained ~3.6x.
- Latency targets: p95 < 220ms for short streaming completions, p99 < 600ms for standard completions; long-form batch can be best-effort.

Let us know if you need higher fidelity token histograms; we can run a 7-day dump.

Thanks,
Daniel

Attachment: hyperscale_workload_sample.csv (csv)
Quoted text:
> On Sun, 13 Dec 2026 at 10:05, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> > Hi Daniel — great to hear and glad the demo landed. Attaching a concise pre-sales questionnaire...

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Wang <daniel@hyperscale.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, procurement@hyperscale.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Hyperscale dedicated sizing — request for commitment/burst matrix and sharding inventory

Thanks for the fast turn, Daniel — the CSV and your answers are perfect. High-level readout / next steps from our side: 

1) Initial sizing approach (conservative):
   - Baseline commit: sized to cover sustained traffic outside peak windows (we'll propose ~60% of sustained 24h average).
   - Burst pool: sized to cover 3.5x sustained for the primary peak window using autoscaling headroom and warm-burst reservations.
   - Mixed GPU mix: for your distribution we recommend a primary pool of 80B quantized variants on A100-type SKUs for streaming short completions, plus a small pool of 33B full-precision for long generations and low-latency p99 fallbacks.

2) Session lifecycle & affinity:
   - We'll treat sessions as ephemeral by default with prefix KV caching for the first 8 tokens preserved in LRU, and provide an option to pin sessions (recommended only for the 8% strict-affinity flows).

3) Sharding / tiling recommendations:
   - Use model-slice sharding where long-form batch jobs are placed on dedicated shards (no KV), and streaming traffic uses multi-tenant shards with affinity tagging. This reduces tail variance and improves packing efficiency.

4) Deliverables we will send tomorrow:
   - Commitment vs Burst matrix (CSV + visual)
   - Projected p95/p99 latency curves for the proposed GPU mix
   - Cost delta for additional burst headroom vs higher base commit

Karthik and Ben will run a short internal probe to validate queueing for the 1,400-token jobs and run a tabletop simulation to verify p99 under 3.6x peak. Can we pencil in a 30-minute handoff call Wednesday 12:00 PST? I'll include a succinct one-page commit recommendation for procurement.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachment: (we'll upload the commitment matrix and projections to the Drive link shared)
